The Wii U has more than enough power to deliver the vision of games that Nintendo wants to produce. Additionally it gives them new input methods to experiment with ways they want to advance gaming.

The problem with this however is that it does not have enough power to deliver the vision of games that most 3rd party developers want to produce; specifically large corporate American developers (EA/Activision/Ubisoft).

Look, Nintendo isn't trying to play the power game, because it's a losing proposition. Just look at PS4 and Xbox one. They duke it out together, and PS4 seems to win the power battle...until you stack it up against PC gaming. So you can't win.

But Nintendo's problem isn't with their mindset, it's with the industry as a whole. Ever since the days of the NES, Nintendo has always provided unique ways to play games. From ROB the robot, to the Zapper, to the NES Advantage. What they expect, however, is that 3rd party developers will take advantage of these unique ways, to make games you simply can't play on other systems. Nintendo doesn't want ports of games that you can find on PS4. They want games that take advantage of the unique hardware. And this is where the industry lets them down. We are now at a point where games have to be so cookie cutter, so risk free, because of the amount of money it takes to make a game. There has to be a guaranteed return on investment...and that investment is too high. Which means that developers have little room to take chances and experiment. To me, that is a huge shame. It means that we won't see a fostering of innovation. It means that all we will have is sequels to the same IPs, and those sequels won't seem like more more than just expansions. Sequels used to mean dramatic changes. Look at Castlevania 1 compared to 2. Zelda 1 compared to 2. Etc. We just aren't seeing those leaps anymore.

As much as I like the Wii U, this article is looking through rose-tinted lenses. Yes, the Wii U is a bastion of couch co-op and good old fashioned gaming fun. It's great to have as a secondary console for when people are over. I own both a PC and a Wii U, and the PC gets used for all serious gaming where the Wii U is just for when friends are over, or one of a few "hardcore" games available to the system.

Its fault is that it that if you are a serious gamer, you can't just own a Wii U; you miss too much, and, the experience is generally better on the PS4/xbone/PC for multi-platform games. Also the online is awful still, at least in my experience. I live in an apartment complex with a bunch of conflicting wi-fi signals so it is probably not really Nintendo's fault beyond not putting a ethernet port on the back, but I still can't use my Wii U for online gaming.

Honestly, the fact that the Wii U's major selling point is that it does what a console should do (allow for couch co-op) shows how far Sony and Microsoft have drifted away from what I look for in a console. I'll probably pick up a PS4 or XBone toward the end of the generation for the few exclusives and as a Netflix machine.

In regards to the internet connection, it's not a perfect solution, but you can still use the Wii LAN adapter if you're desperate for a wired connection.

In all honesty, come the next generation I might just opt for PC and NX. The only thing really keeping me to the other consoles is I still kinda like Halo, and some of the Sony exclusive stuff is interesting, but I don't think that's going to be enough to convince me next time.

I'll start off by saying this is all just my opinion. The suggestions are just something I think will help make the server better.

This server has been nothing but fantastic so far. Everyone is nice, always someone there to help answer questions, the mods are on point and it's just nice to see a new community working so well so quickly. I do have a few suggestions though.

Aside from placing your chest in a claimed area, you have no protection on it. Maybe something like LWC can help out with this. You can lock chests, unlock them to the public, set passwords on them, set them to work for certain groups of people, etc... Pretty much every server I have played on has had it along with Core Protect so that am admin or mod with permissions can see what has been taken from the chest and when. It would keep everyone's items safe if they can't place a chest in a claimed area, or haven't claimed an area yet.

Towns. I understand the wanting to keep the game close to vanilla as possible, and I love that, but the only "town" we have now is Tropia. I have nothing against Tropia. It's a great place for beginner players to get some food if they need it, or even use the enchanting table if they haven't gotten the required materials for one yet. It's just that it's the only place like it. I know that everything is still fairly new, but unless you play for a while, you can't gain enough land to claim to create a town or you have to just create your own town with friends and just live next to each other and give each other perms to build. Towny could help this, but only if it was implemented in the right way. It would require an economy plugin though (I know that has been talked about). If you know some of the not so common commands for Towny, it can be a very useful plugin to create not just towns, but nations, capitols, allies/foes etc... It can also provide a money sink for the server to pull some excess money out of the economy by having a daily tax or upkeep cost for a town.

There's more, but this is already lengthy and I don't want to bore the crap out of anyone (plus I have to start getting ready for work). I'll add to this later and would love some comments about what I mentioned or even other suggestions.
